overview: eBay operates a global online marketplace connecting buyers and sellers across www.ebay.com and localized international sites, plus a suite of mobile apps, generating revenue primarily from seller transaction fees (final value fees) and advertising. The company has repositioned from a broad, low-differentiation marketplace toward 'Focused Categories' (collectibles, motors parts and accessories, fashion, refurbished/electronics) and the C2C/recommerce space, culminating in the July 2026 acquisition of Depop, a mobile-first fashion resale marketplace popular with Gen Z. eBay generates roughly half its GMV from cross-border/international trade, making it more exposed than most US e-commerce peers to tariff and de minimis policy changes.

business_model.summary: eBay operates a single reportable segment (the Marketplace) monetized through two revenue streams: Marketplace revenue (final value fees, listing/feature fees, store subscriptions, shipping and payments-related fees) and a fast-growing, high-margin Advertising revenue stream (first-party promoted listings plus third-party ads). FY2025 revenue was $11.10B (+8% YoY): Marketplace revenue $9,107M (+5%) and Advertising revenue $1,993M (+22%). Take rate expansion via advertising is the central margin lever, since ad revenue carries minimal incremental cost. Q2 2026 first-party advertising revenue alone reached $570M (+25% YoY). The July 2026 Depop acquisition ($1.4B closed; originally announced at ~$1.2B) adds a second, younger-skewing C2C fashion marketplace to the portfolio.

revenue_streams.name: Marketplace (transaction/final value fees, listing, store subscriptions, shipping)

business_model.customer_type: C2C and small/medium business sellers (largely SMB, individual/hobbyist, and professional resellers) selling to a global base of individual buyers; increasingly skewed toward 'Focused Category' enthusiast buyers (collectibles, motors parts, trading cards, sneakers, watches) rather than generic new-goods retail
business_model.geographic_mix: Roughly half of GMV is generated outside the US, with meaningful cross-border trade flows (e.g., items shipped between US, UK, Germany, and other markets), making eBay unusually exposed to tariffs, de minimis policy, and FX relative to domestically-focused US e-commerce peers

competitive_position.market_position: A distant #2 to Amazon in overall US e-commerce GMV (Amazon ~48% share of e-commerce vs. eBay's low-single-digit to ~7% share by some estimates), but eBay has repositioned away from head-to-head competition with Amazon in commoditized new goods toward category leadership in used, collectible, and enthusiast goods (trading cards, motors parts, luxury watches, sneakers, refurbished electronics) where it retains structural advantages (auction format, authentication, long-tail inventory, seller tools).

moat_factors.factor: Two-sided network effects in niche/collectible categories
moat_factors.description: Decades of accumulated long-tail, hard-to-find inventory (parts, collectibles, vintage items) create liquidity that is difficult for new entrants to replicate; sellers list where buyers already search, and buyers search where the most unique/used inventory exists.

Authenticity Guarantee (expanded to 100+ fashion brands, plus trading cards, sneakers, watches, and handbags) and buyer/seller protection programs reduce fraud risk in a market (used/collectible goods) where trust is the primary barrier to transacting with strangers.

First-party promoted listings ad business ($570M in Q2 2026 alone, +25% YoY) monetizes eBay's own search intent data without needing third-party ad tech, expanding take rate with minimal incremental cost.

eBay remains a top-of-mind destination for selling used goods and collectibles, though brand strength has eroded somewhat versus newer, more curated apps (Poshmark, Depop, Mercari) among younger demographics — a gap the Depop acquisition is explicitly intended to close.

Established international shipping, currency conversion, and payments rails (eBay's own managed payments platform) support cross-border trade at scale, though this is also a source of tariff/regulatory risk.

weaknesses: Legacy 'general merchandise' marketplace perception persists among consumers who default to Amazon for new goods, structurally capping eBay's addressable share of overall e-commerce
Weaker mobile-native/social commerce experience than newer resale apps (Depop, Vinted, Poshmark) among Gen Z, which is why eBay chose to acquire rather than build that experience
Cross-border GMV (~half of total) is disproportionately exposed to de minimis and tariff policy changes that peers with more domestic-only GMV largely avoid

Long-run active buyer/seller growth has been roughly flat to low-single-digit for years, with growth increasingly reliant on GMV/take-rate mix shift (Focused Categories, advertising) rather than marketplace expansion

AI/agentic shopping assistants (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google) risk disintermediating eBay's own search and discovery layer if buyers increasingly transact through third-party AI agents rather than the eBay app/site directly

growth_drivers: Focused Categories strategy: collectibles, motors parts & accessories, fashion (including luxury), and refurbished/electronics now represent over 40% of total GMV and are each growing faster than the marketplace average (focused-category GMV +26% in Q2 2026)
Strategic priorities (Focused Categories + C2C + recommerce) collectively drove over 70% of total GMV growth in Q2 2026, each growing 20%+

Depop acquisition (closed July 30, 2026, ~$1.4B): adds a fast-growing, Gen Z-skewed fashion resale marketplace (~$1B GMS in 2025, +~60% YoY in the US) expected to contribute 1.5-2.5 points to consolidated GMV/revenue growth in FY2026, with revenue synergies from cross-promotion and eBay's authentication/logistics infrastructure
eBay Live (livestream shopping/auctions): GMV grew roughly eightfold YoY across seven markets in Q2 2026, an emerging high-engagement format for collectibles and trading cards

Advertising take-rate expansion: first-party ad revenue +25% YoY in Q2 2026 ($570M), still under-monetized relative to Amazon's ad business as a percent of GMV, representing a multi-year margin/revenue lever

AI-powered seller and buyer tools (AI-powered listing creation, search relevance/refinements) management says are driving ~50% more search engagement, positioned as a structural tailwind rather than an agentic-AI disintermediation threat
Authenticity Guarantee expansion (now 100+ fashion brands plus trading cards, watches, sneakers) increasing trust and enabling higher-value/luxury GMV
Continued capital return: active buyback program (~$2.0B remaining authorization as of Q2 2026) plus a quarterly dividend, both supporting EPS growth ahead of revenue growth

business.description: Amazon's scale, Prime ecosystem, and broader assortment continue to pressure eBay's relevance for mainstream/new-goods shopping, limiting TAM expansion outside eBay's resale/collectibles niche.

LLM-driven shopping agents (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini) could increasingly mediate product discovery and purchase decisions, bypassing eBay's own site/app and search-driven ad monetization. eBay has already moved to block autonomous 'buy-for-me' AI agents from its checkout (effective Feb 20, 2026), a defensive stance that could also cede future agentic-commerce volume to competitors who embrace it.

A ~$1.4B acquisition of a culturally distinct, community-driven app carries brand-dilution and integration risk if eBay's systems/processes are imposed too heavily on Depop's community-first culture, echoing risks seen in other marketplace M&A (e.g., Etsy's own struggles integrating Depop and Elo7 before divesting Depop to eBay).

Poshmark, Vinted, Mercari, and (pre-acquisition) Depop have captured younger, fashion-focused resale demand with lower fees or more social/curated experiences, requiring eBay to compete on user experience, not just liquidity.

financial.description: With roughly half of GMV international, reported revenue and GMV growth diverge from FX-neutral growth (e.g., Q2 2026 was 15% as-reported vs. 14% FX-neutral); a stronger dollar is a headwind to reported results.

Management guided that Depop will dilute full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS by up to 2.5 points even as it adds 1.5-2.5 points of GMV/revenue growth, reflecting near-term integration costs and Depop's earlier-stage margin profile.

financial.risk: Capital allocation to buybacks/dividend vs. reinvestment
financial.description: eBay returned $448M to shareholders in Q2 2026 alone ($310M buybacks + $138M dividends) with $2.0B of authorization remaining; heavy capital return is a positive for EPS but leaves less capacity for further large M&A without added leverage.

regulatory.risk: De minimis and tariff policy changes
regulatory.description: The $800 de minimis exemption for low-value imports was eliminated for China/Hong Kong in mid-2025 and suspended globally in August 2025, with tariffs/flat fees (up to 120% ad valorem or $100-200 flat per item) now applying broadly to cross-border parcels. Given eBay's substantial cross-border GMV, this raises landed costs for buyers and could dampen cross-border transaction volume, though eBay has also noted some sellers/marketplaces gain relative competitiveness versus Chinese direct-to-consumer platforms (Temu, Shein, AliExpress) that relied even more heavily on de minimis.

regulatory.risk: Marketplace liability / product safety and IP enforcement
regulatory.description: As a facilitator of C2C and cross-border trade, eBay faces ongoing regulatory scrutiny globally (EU Digital Services Act, US product-safety and counterfeit-goods enforcement) around seller verification, counterfeit listings, and marketplace liability.
eBay's managed payments platform and global data flows are subject to evolving payments regulation (PSD2-style rules in the EU) and data privacy regimes (GDPR, US state privacy laws).

macro.description: GMV is tied to discretionary spending on used/collectible/non-essential goods; a consumer pullback in a slowing macro environment could pressure both buyer demand and average selling prices.
Limited direct sensitivity given eBay's asset-light model and strong free cash flow, though equity valuation multiples for the stock are influenced by the broader rate environment.
Escalating US-China trade tensions and reciprocal tariffs affect cross-border GMV flows in both directions (US buyers importing from abroad and international buyers purchasing from US sellers).

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global e-commerce and resale/recommerce markets continue to grow structurally, with the secondhand/recommerce category growing faster than overall retail as sustainability awareness, price sensitivity, and Gen Z resale culture expand the addressable market. eBay estimates it generated $5.3B in positive economic impact through recommerce in 2025.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. GMV is tied to discretionary consumer spending and correlates with broader retail/e-commerce cycles, but the value/resale positioning (used goods, refurbished electronics, deal-seeking) provides some counter-cyclical buffer relative to full-price new-goods retailers during downturns.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct operational sensitivity (asset-light, strong FCF generation, modest debt load) but moderate valuation sensitivity as a mature-growth tech/e-commerce name.

recent_developments.event: eBay completed its acquisition of Depop from Etsy for approximately $1.4 billion in cash, adding the Gen Z-focused fashion resale marketplace (~$1B GMS in 2025, +~60% YoY US growth) to its portfolio; deal was announced in February 2026.

Q2 2026 earnings: revenue $3.1B (+15% YoY, +14% FX-neutral), GMV $22.4B (+15% YoY), both beating guidance. GAAP diluted EPS $1.21; non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.60 (+17% YoY), beating the $1.46-1.51 guide. GAAP operating margin 21.6% (up from 17.6% a year earlier); non-GAAP operating margin 28.5%. Strategic priorities (Focused Categories + C2C + recommerce) drove over 70% of GMV growth, each growing 20%+; Focused Category GMV grew 26% and surpassed 40% of total GMV for the first time. First-party advertising revenue reached $570M (+25% YoY). eBay Live GMV grew roughly 8x YoY across seven markets. Company returned $448M to shareholders ($310M buybacks, $138M dividends), with $2.0B of buyback authorization remaining.

Management raised full-year 2026 guidance: GMV growth of 11.5-12.5% FX-neutral, revenue growth of 11-12%, non-GAAP operating income and EPS both guided to 10-12% growth, citing broad-based business momentum. Depop is expected to add 1.5-2.5 points to GMV/revenue growth for FY2026 but dilute non-GAAP EPS by up to 2.5 points.

eBay implemented a policy prohibiting third-party AI/agentic 'buy-for-me' bots from autonomously placing orders on its platform, updating its user agreement to require human review for all purchases, a defensive posture against ungoverned agentic-commerce flows even as management frames AI-assisted search/discovery as a growth driver.

eBay announced the definitive agreement to acquire Depop from Etsy for approximately $1.2 billion (deal terms/consideration finalized at ~$1.4B by closing in July 2026), explicitly targeting fashion (a >$10B annual GMV category for eBay, +10% YoY in the US in 2025) and a younger demographic underrepresented in eBay's core marketplace.

US de minimis duty-free treatment (the $800 exemption) was eliminated for China/Hong Kong shipments in May 2025 and suspended globally in August 2025, materially raising the cost of low-value cross-border parcels; eBay published seller guidance on tariff pass-through and updated its cross-border trade tools in response, given roughly half of its GMV is cross-border.

StoneX analyst raised the eBay price target to $136 (from $134) while reiterating a Buy rating, part of a broader mixed analyst picture (1 Strong Buy, 14 Buy, 17 Hold, 2 Sell) with an average consensus price target of approximately $117 as of mid-September 2026, modestly above the ~$113 trading price.

items.notes: Raised following a Q2 2026 beat (GMV +15% as-reported, +14% FX-neutral vs. $21.3-21.7B guide). Includes ~1.5-2.5 points of contribution from the Depop acquisition (closed July 30, 2026).
Q2 2026 revenue of $3.13B beat the $2.97-3.03B guide; Depop expected to add 1.5-2.5 points of revenue growth.
Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating income of $893M beat the $820-850M guide; non-GAAP operating margin reached 28.5% in Q2.
Depop expected to dilute non-GAAP EPS by up to 2.5 points for the full year, partially offsetting core-business EPS growth; Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $1.60 (+17% YoY) beat the $1.46-1.51 guide.
Implies deceleration versus Q2's 14% FX-neutral growth, partly reflecting tougher prior-year comps.
First quarter to include a partial period of Depop consolidation (deal closed July 30, 2026).

guidance.management_commentary: CFO Peggy Alford said the company is 'increasing our full-year top- and bottom-line outlook' based on observed business momentum across strategic priorities. CEO Jamie Iannone emphasized 'focused execution against our strategic roadmap,' highlighting Focused Categories surpassing 40% of GMV, eBay Live's roughly eightfold GMV growth, and the strategic rationale for Depop as accelerating eBay's push into fashion/recommerce and reaching a younger buyer demographic. Management continues to frame AI-assisted search and listing tools as a growth driver (citing ~50% higher search engagement) while taking a defensive posture on ungoverned third-party AI purchasing agents.

bull_case: Successful strategic pivot from commoditized general merchandise to defensible, higher-growth Focused Categories (collectibles, motors, fashion, refurbished) now exceeding 40% of GMV and outgrowing the core marketplace, supported by high-margin, fast-growing first-party advertising revenue (+25% YoY)

Depop acquisition meaningfully expands eBay's addressable market in fashion resale and Gen Z demographics at a reasonable ~$1.4B price relative to the ~$1B GMS asset acquired, with clear cross-sell/authentication synergies

Consistent guidance beats and raises through FY2026 (GMV, revenue, operating income, and EPS all raised after Q2), with expanding operating margins (GAAP margin up ~400bps YoY in Q2) showing the business is scaling profitably, not just growing top line

Disciplined, substantial capital return program ($448M returned in a single quarter, $2.0B of buyback authorization remaining) supports EPS growth and provides valuation support at a stock trading well below its historical highs
eBay Live and AI-powered seller/search tools represent emerging, largely unmonetized growth vectors (eBay Live GMV +~8x YoY) that could become more material contributors over a multi-year horizon
bear_case: Structural exposure to de minimis/tariff policy changes (roughly half of GMV is cross-border) creates an ongoing overhang not shared by more domestically-focused US e-commerce peers, with the 2025 elimination of the $800 exemption already raising landed costs for cross-border buyers

Long-run active buyer growth has been largely stagnant for years; growth is increasingly a function of GMV/take-rate mix shift (Focused Categories, advertising) rather than genuine marketplace expansion, raising questions about the durability of double-digit growth once easy comps and the Depop contribution roll off

Agentic AI commerce (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google shopping agents) poses a longer-term disintermediation risk to eBay's search/discovery-driven advertising model; eBay's defensive stance of blocking third-party AI purchasing agents could cede ground to competitors who embrace agentic checkout flows

Depop integration carries brand and execution risk — Etsy itself struggled to realize value from Depop before divesting it, and near-term EPS dilution (up to 2.5 points in FY2026) shows the deal is not immediately accretive

Consensus analyst view remains a lukewarm 'Hold' (1 Strong Buy, 14 Buy, 17 Hold, 2 Sell) with an average price target only modestly above the trading price, reflecting persistent skepticism about eBay's ability to sustain growth rates against Amazon's scale and newer resale-native competitors
